title: Google Brings Agentic AI to Hotel Search Inside Maps
excerpt: Ask Maps now lets travelers describe what they want in a hotel — vibe, proximity, budget — and get real-time pricing and availability, with itinerary integration on the way.
body:
• Google Maps' Ask Maps feature now supports AI-powered hotel search with real-time pricing and availability
  • Travelers can describe preferences like vibe, proximity, and budget in natural language instead of using rigid filters
  • The feature builds on Google's agentic AI rollout that already handles restaurant reservations via OpenTable and Resy in the US, India, UK, Canada, and Australia

Google Maps is adding AI-powered hotel search to a surface already built around location, transit, routes, and nearby businesses. Through the Ask Maps feature, travelers can now use conversational queries to find hotels based on specific feel, proximity to venues, and budget — and receive actual pricing and availability rather than estimates, according to Skift.

How It Works

The update moves hotel discovery beyond the traditional filter-and-sort approach. Google's example prompt: "For next week's conference in downtown Miami, find me a decently priced, top-rated hotel with an artsy vibe, within walking distance from a gym and restaurants." The AI interprets these layered preferences and returns results with real pricing data.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PMIZm3alM0o

Maps can also layer in a traveler's own itinerary, potentially matching hotel location to planned activities and meetings. This spatial context — knowing where you need to be and when — sets the feature apart from standalone hotel search engines.

Part of a Broader Agentic Push

The hotel search capability extends Google's agentic AI strategy that has been unfolding since late 2025. AI Mode in Search already generates structured travel itineraries through the Canvas tool, combining flights, hotels, and activities into an editable side panel.

Agentic booking for restaurants — where AI Mode searches across platforms like OpenTable, Resy, and Tock for real-time availability — is live in the US and has expanded to the UK, India, Canada, and Australia. Event tickets and local appointment booking through partners like Ticketmaster, StubHub, and Booksy are available to US Labs users.

Hotel Price Tracking Gets Granular

Alongside the AI search features, Google has added individual hotel price tracking. Users can now track price changes for a specific property rather than monitoring rates at the city level. On desktop, a price-tracking toggle appears when searching by hotel name; on mobile, it is available in the Prices tab. Email alerts are sent when prices change for selected dates.

The feature launched globally for signed-in users in English and Spanish, according to Google's blog.

What Is Missing

Direct hotel booking within AI Mode is not yet available. Google confirmed it is working with industry partners including Booking.com and Expedia to add flight and hotel reservations directly to AI Mode, but provided no timeline. For now, hotel results link out to booking partners rather than completing transactions within Google's interface.

"Queries in Google's AI mode are three times longer than traditional search queries."

— Skift, reporting on Google's earnings call

What It Means for Travel

The integration matters because it keeps the entire discovery-to-decision flow inside a surface travelers already use for navigation and local search. Rather than switching between Maps for location context and a separate booking site for availability, the two are now converging. If Google adds personal itinerary data and completes the booking loop, Ask Maps could become a primary hotel search tool — handling the where, what, and how much in a single conversational thread.
